oidc_jwt.description: Invalid response_mode values on the authorization endpoint are ignored and ZITADEL falls back to the default response mode for the response_type/application configuration.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid flagging fallback behavior as flow confusion or parameter tampering acceptance.

oidc_jwt.description: The redirect_uri in code exchange must exactly match the redirect_uri used in the authorization request and a preregistered URI.
oidc_jwt.note: Mismatch failures are by-design flow binding checks.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo and introspection return only claims allowed by granted scopes; many profile/email/roles/metadata claims are omitted unless requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing optional claims are by design and should not be treated as identity corruption or privilege stripping.

oidc_jwt.description: Token introspection reports active=true only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive result from a non-audience client is expected and not evidence of revocation or token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token requests may only ask for a scope subset of the original authorization; broader scopes are rejected.
oidc_jwt.note: Scope expansion failure on refresh is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange audience must be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejected exchanges to unrelated audiences are by design.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo and introspection only return many claims when the corresponding scopes were granted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing email/profile/roles/metadata claims as under- or over-binding unless the relevant scopes were requested.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT access tokens include all client IDs and the project ID in aud by default, and reserved scopes can add more audiences.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat these documented audiences as unintended escalation.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange rejects scopes that exceed those granted by the resource owner with invalid_scope.
oidc_jwt.note: This is expected enforcement, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer grant assertions are documented as signed JWTs with exp/iat requirements, but the docs do not describe jti replay tracking or one-time-use semantics for assertions.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability solely because it can be reused; absent documented jti tracking, this is not evidence of an I2 violation.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include RFC7523-required claims aud, exp, iat, iss, sub, and the JOSE header MUST include kid matching the downloaded key ID. ZITADEL requires aud to include the issuing domain and requires iat to be no older than 1 hour. Use control assertions with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed assertion setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For I1 signature-validation tests on login_with_jwt, ZITADEL validates the JWT bearer assertion against a previously downloaded/generated private-key-backed service-account key and identifies the key via the JWT header kid. kid injection tests must vary kid while keeping the rest of the assertion valid; missing or wrong kid can fail as normal key lookup failure rather than exposing a signature-verification flaw.

replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti are BY-DESIGN non-findings for login_with_jwt. The documentation for the JWT profile grant requires signed assertions with exp/iat but does not document jti submission or one-time-use tracking. Do NOT flag successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as an I2 vulnerability unless the platform explicitly documents replay prevention for this grant.

For start_oidc_auth, redirect_uri matching is exact and must equal a preregistered callback URI. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the baseline and attack must differ only in the intended mismatch dimension; otherwise ZITADEL will reject the request as normal invalid_grant/invalid_request behavior due to exact redirect_uri enforcement.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do NOT test alternate PKCE methods as security findings. For pkce_skip and code-injection/state-swap style tests, use a valid S256 baseline first; otherwise failures may be caused by unsupported PKCE method rather than session binding.

For exchange_code_for_token, the required client-auth parameters depend on the chosen auth method: PKCE uses client_id + code_verifier; client_secret_basic uses Authorization header; private_key_jwt uses client_assertion + client_assertion_type. The fuzzer MUST keep the auth method consistent between baseline and attack sequences. Mixing methods causes expected token-endpoint rejection and is not an I3 coherence issue.

For start_oidc_auth, response_mode invalid values are ignored and ZITADEL chooses a default based on response_type. Do NOT treat fallback to default response_mode as a bug. Tests that depend on where parameters are returned must explicitly request a supported response_mode (query, fragment, form_post) and verify the returned location accordingly.

For I5 scope-tightening and token-exchange tests, openid is mandatory for OIDC requests and refresh-token scopes must be a subset of the original scope. Token exchange scope requests are documented as requested scopes and invalid_scope is returned when they exceed authorization. The fuzzer MUST include a valid baseline scope set and compare against a narrowed or expanded attack request; otherwise rejection may simply be due to missing mandatory openid or invalid scope syntax.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, audience must be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. ZITADEL documents this explicitly. Therefore, a rejected exchange with a foreign audience is expected behavior, not a bug. A valid I5 test must first obtain a subject token whose audience legitimately includes the target audience, then attempt a disallowed expansion beyond that subset.

For token_exchange token-type tests, only documented token-type combinations are valid: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. The fuzzer MUST use only supported combinations for baseline tests and treat unsupported combinations as setup errors, not security findings.

For verify_granted_identity, claims returned depend on granted scopes. preferred_username, email, profile fields, roles, and metadata may be absent unless the corresponding scopes were granted. I4/I5 verification logic MUST compare only claims requested by scope or always-present claims such as sub; otherwise missing claims can create false identity-mismatch or privilege-loss positives.

For introspect_token, active=true additionally requires that the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST introspect with the same client context that obtained or is in the audience of the token. Otherwise active=false or 401 invalid_client is expected and must not be interpreted as token revocation or audience-binding failure.

For revoke_session and introspect_token, client authentication is required by the endpoint documentation ('depending on your authorization method'). The fuzzer MUST supply a valid client authentication method consistent with the application configuration. A 401 invalid_client is a setup/authentication failure, not evidence about token validity or revocation semantics.

No documented numeric sentinel semantics were found for token lifetimes, leeway, use-count, or expiry configuration parameters in the provided OIDC/JWT docs. Do NOT assume 0 means default, disable, or strict mode for any tested parameter without separate platform documentation.

For I2 freshness tests against /oauth/v2/token using the JWT bearer grant, the JWT assertion MUST include exp and iat, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control tokens; expired-token attacks should set exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} and future/not-yet-valid attacks should rely on token claims being checked by ZITADEL.

For I1 JWT-bearer tests, the JWT header MUST include kid matching the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL uses kid to identify which registered key to validate against; missing or attacker-chosen unknown kid causes rejection for setup reasons rather than proving deeper signature-validation behavior.

For I1 issuer/audience validation of JWT bearer assertions, the assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain exactly as documented (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}). If aud is wrong or omitted, login fails as invalid setup and cannot distinguish issuer/trust-anchor failures from audience failures.

For I2 expired_token and future_token sequences, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT bearer assertion in the same environment. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication, wrong kid, wrong aud, or wrong service-account key setup.

For I3 authorization-code coherence tests, redirect_uri at /oauth/v2/token MUST match exactly the redirect_uri used at /oauth/v2/authorize. A mismatch yields invalid_grant by design and must not be interpreted as a session-binding or state-binding vulnerability.

For PKCE-based code exchange tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do not send plain or other methods; failures would be due to unsupported PKCE method, not a security property under test.

For OIDC authorization requests, response_mode invalid values are ignored by ZITADEL. Do not treat fallback behavior as a flow-coherence bug; when testing response handling, assert against the effective default mode for the chosen response_type.

For I3 state-swap and code-injection style tests, preserve all original query parameters across redirects/proxies. The JWT IdP documentation explicitly requires forwarding all original query parameters intact to preserve OIDC flow state; dropping or mutating them creates setup-induced failures.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, audience in token exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. Requests outside that subset are rejected by design and should not be reported as inconsistent authorization binding.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh_token grant MUST be a subset of the originally granted scope, and token-exchange scope is explicitly requested at the token endpoint. Any rejection for expanded scope can be by-design scope enforcement rather than a bug; compare exchanged token claims only when the request itself is valid under documented subset rules.

For I5 token-exchange token-type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt as subject_token is allowed only with actor_token; user_id subject token is allowed only with actor_token. Unsupported combinations must not be flagged as authorization failures.

For verify_granted_identity, /oidc/v1/userinfo only accepts access tokens of a user as Bearer tokens, not client-only tokens. Do not call userinfo with client_credentials or other non-user tokens and interpret 401 as identity confusion.

For introspection-based verification, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. If the introspecting client is not in aud, inactive/authorization failure is by design and must not be treated as token invalidity or revocation.

Reserved scope matching in ZITADEL is exact-string and exact-template based. Scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id} do not document wildcard or regex support. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, OMIT these exact-binding scopes unless the test intentionally targets that exact org/domain/project/idp; setting '*' would be treated literally, not as a wildcard.

For I5 authorization-binding tests using reserved scopes, requesting urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud intentionally adds that project id to the access-token audience. Do not include this scope in baseline tests unless the audience expansion is the behavior under test, or you may create false positives for over-broad audience grants.

For I5 org-membership tests, requesting urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} causes ZITADEL to enforce organization membership by design. Rejections under these scopes are expected membership checks, not generic authentication failures.

For JWT IdP upstream testing through ZITADEL's OIDC flow, the upstream JWT must be delivered in an HTTP header, never as a URL parameter. Tests that place the JWT in query parameters are invalid against documented behavior and any rejection is by design.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain, iss equal to sub, a kid header matching the downloaded keyId, and iat no older than 1 hour. Without these baseline requirements, token rejection is ambiguous and not attributable to exp/nbf freshness checks.

For I2 token-freshness tests on login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid assertion alongside the ATTACK login. A safe control is exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, sub/iss set to the service account or client identifier, aud set to the issuer domain, and a valid kid. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED may reflect broken JWT construction rather than freshness enforcement.

ZITADEL JWT profile grant is for service accounts and requires a ZITADEL-generated private key. Do NOT treat replay of the same JWT bearer assertion as a guaranteed vulnerability signal: the docs do not describe jti tracking or one-time assertion enforcement for this grant. replay_same_token is at best a hardening check unless the same assertion is documented as single-use elsewhere.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL requires an exact match and returns invalid_grant otherwise; this is by design and should be asserted as flow binding, not identity confusion.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, start_oidc_auth MUST set code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256, and exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier with client_id. ZITADEL documents S256 as the only supported code_challenge_method. Any other method or missing verifier causes rejection by design.

For I3 pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client checks, assert only that exchange_code_for_token returns a non-success status or OAuth error when code_verifier is omitted after a PKCE authorization request. Do NOT compare identities across users; this is a flow-rejection test.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, token_exchange audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If you request an audience outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of over-granting.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, token_exchange scope MUST be interpreted relative to upstream authorization. ZITADEL documents invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. The fuzzer MUST compare requested exchanged scope against the original token scope and treat rejection as correct behavior.

For token_exchange type tests, subject_token_type, actor_token_type, and requested_token_type MUST use only documented supported combinations. In particular: refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token or actor_token; requested_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; token-type jwt as subject_token is only allowed with actor_token; user_id subject_token is only allowed with actor_token. Unsupported combinations will fail by design.

For I5 tests using verify_granted_identity, UserInfo returns claims depending on granted scopes. Missing email/profile/roles/metadata claims without corresponding scopes is by design. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes before asserting absence or presence of those claims as an authorization-binding result.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, ZITADEL by default includes all client IDs and the project ID in aud for JWT access tokens, and additional audiences can be requested via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud. The fuzzer MUST account for these documented audience-expanding scopes when evaluating whether an audience was over-granted.

For I5 organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} causes ZITADEL to enforce organization membership. Rejection under these scopes is expected if the user is not a member or the username/domain does not match; do not misclassify this as a generic login failure.

For I3 and I5 tests involving response_mode, invalid response_mode values are ignored by ZITADEL. The fuzzer MUST NOT rely on an invalid response_mode to force a specific callback transport or to infer inconsistent flow handling.

For JWT IdP browser-proxy scenarios relevant to OIDC login initiation, the proxy to /idps/jwt MUST forward all original query parameters intact and place the JWT in the configured HTTP header, not a URL parameter. If query parameters are dropped, OIDC state is broken by setup error rather than broker flaw.
